note: Pathfinding over dug and built ground (roadmap item 49; core/game/game_path.gd, checked by tools/check_data.gd). A* over the cells of the world: the surface (layer y = -1, one cell for each tile of the generated world, with its height) and the ground under it (y = 0 and down, the cells GameMine says are dug). A mover steps between cells that its kind can stand on (`movers`): a walker climbs a few heights and drops a few more, keeps off open water, and is stopped by trees and rock outcrops; a climber takes cliffs; a swimmer crosses water; a flier crosses anything on the surface. Terrain costs time (`terrain`: forest and swamp are slow), a slope costs more, a diagonal costs more and may not cut a corner, and climbing up a shaft costs more than going down it. Digging changes the ground (a dug cell can be walked, so a tunnel is a way round a wall), and building changes it too: a `built` overlay says which cells hold a wall (solid), a floor, a road (quick) or a door (slow), so item 50's buildings only have to fill it in. The search is bounded by `max_nodes`; if it cannot reach the goal it gives the way to the nearest cell it did reach, so a creature can still move toward what it cannot get to. Nothing here is saved or random.
